annotation.title_clean: Opinion: Uses of Copyrighted Materials for Machine Learning
annotation.title_en: Opinion: Uses of Copyrighted Materials for Machine Learning
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Israel Ministry of Justice, Legislation and Legal Counsel (Civil Law)
annotation.summary_en: Israeli Ministry of Justice legal opinion concluding that using copyrighted works to train machine learning models is generally permitted under existing Israeli copyright law, chiefly via fair use, plus incidental use and transient copying. It excludes single-author style-mimicry datasets and model outputs, and prefers interpretive guidance over legislation.
key_provisions_or_claims: ML training on copyrighted works is typically fair use under section 19 of the Israeli Copyright Act 2007.
Incidental use (s.22) and transient copying (s.26) may apply in some circumstances.
Dataset diversity is proposed as a new fair use factor.
Safe harbor excludes datasets of a single author's works used to compete with that author, and does not cover outputs.
Recommends relying on existing law rather than legislative amendment for now.
